audit.title: Chainlink VRF

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Opens with a self-contained definition: "provably fair and verifiable random number generator (RNG) that enables smart contracts to access random values…" Each H2 also leads with its answer. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; 4 clean sections, no level skips, one well-formed comparison table, all sections under 600 words. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 11 numerals, **0 with units**, 0 hex addresses. Claims like "more random values returned per single request" and "reduced gas overhead" are qualitative; the actual limits are punted to another page. This is the largest scored gap.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Moderate. 4 external links but **0 to primary sources** — the VRF paper / cryptographic spec for the "verifiable random function" claim is absent; externals are blog/Twitter/StackOverflow.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Strong. The bold lead sentence and the adversary-caveat footnote are both cleanly liftable.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. No JSON-LD/`TechArticle`, no canonical URL, no `dateModified`. (Head not captured — CLI should pass raw `<head>` to confirm, but the served HTML carried none.)

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Weak by rubric (0 code blocks). Acceptable for a pure overview page, but a minimal "request randomness" snippet or explicit pointer would raise agent utility.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Moderate. Covers "what is VRF," "which method," "supported networks." No troubleshooting, no FAQ, no symptom/error phrasing — misses agents querying by failure mode.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Consistent "VRF v2.5" naming, unambiguous prose. Minor: one table cell says "V2 direct funding supported networks" where "V2.5" is meant.

audit.summary: This is the top-level Chainlink VRF overview page: a strong canonical definition, a clean subscription-vs-direct-funding comparison table, and clear routing to deeper pages. Its biggest GEO strength is the crisp, liftable opening definition and the decision table an engine can extract *reasons* from; its biggest opportunity is the near-total absence of concrete numbers (every quantitative claim is deferred to "Supported networks") and missing machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical, no dates). Honest verdict: a well-written hub that under-indexes on specifics and structured metadata — solidly Developing, one metadata + specifics pass away from Good.

recommendations.title: Add machine-readable metadata
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `about: "Chainlink VRF"`, and a canonical `<link rel="canonical" href="https://docs.chain.link/vrf">`. Surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-trust (E-E-A-T) and citation eligibility for agents.

recommendations.title: Pull key numeric limits onto the page
recommendations.issue: "More random values returned per single request" (no number); all limits deferred.
recommendations.change: State the canonical maxima inline, e.g. "Subscription returns up to 500 random values per request; direct funding fewer due to higher gas overhead," plus a representative max gas limit. Keep the link for full per-network tables.
recommendations.why: Quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes; qualitative-only prose underperforms in retrieval and synthesis.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/intent-phrased entry points
recommendations.where: new short section or FAQ near the bottom
recommendations.issue: No "how do I…" or error-phrased headings; agents query by symptom.
recommendations.change: Add H2/H3s such as "How do I request randomness with VRF v2.5?", "Should I use subscription or direct funding?", "Why is my VRF request not fulfilled?" — each answering in the first sentence and linking deeper.
recommendations.why: Symptom/question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Cite a primary source for the RNG claim
recommendations.issue: "0 to primary sources"; "verifiable random function" is uncited.
recommendations.change: Inline-link the VRF cryptographic paper/spec at first use of "Verifiable Random Function."
recommendations.why: Authoritative primary references raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Fix the V2/V2.5 label inconsistency
recommendations.issue: "V2 direct funding supported networks" link text
recommendations.change: Change to "V2.5 direct funding supported networks."
recommendations.why: Consistent version naming aids entity resolution and prevents an engine surfacing stale-version guidance.

recommendations.title: Add one minimal linked code path
recommendations.issue: 0 code blocks; agents get no runnable anchor from the hub.
recommendations.change: Add a 3–5 line Solidity request snippet (or an explicit "Get a random number" quickstart link) labeled by language/network.
recommendations.why: Complete, labeled snippets raise agent-runnability even on overview pages.

antiPatterns: Deferred specifics: quantitative claims ("more random values," "reduced gas overhead") repeatedly pointed off-page rather than stated — weakens standalone chunk value.
Minor version-label inconsistency ("V2" vs "V2.5") in the table.
No stale-content risk detected, but no visible date to prove freshness either.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this page is indexed there.
Head metadata could not be verified from the served content; have the CLI pass raw `<head>` for a definitive metadata read before treating schema as absent.
Concrete per-network limits live on the linked "Supported networks" page; internal links into this hub from that page (canonical-hub pattern) would reinforce retrieval.
